source: In 22% of our films, actresses had the most amount of dialogue (i.e., they were the lead).
claim: Actors have the most dialogue in 78.2% of films and actresses in 21.8%.

source: The most abysmal stat is when women occupy at least 2 of the top 3 roles in a film, which occurs in 18% of our films. That same scenario for men occurs in about 82% of films.
claim: Men occupy at least two of the top three dialogue roles in 81.95% of films and women in 17.95%.

source: The amount of dialogue, by age-range, is completely opposite for women versus men. Dialogue available to women who are over 40 years old decrease substantially. For men, it’s the exact opposite: there are more roles available to older actors.
claim: Female characters' words are 7.81% under 21, 37.50% at 21-31, 31.62% at 32-41, 19.99% at 42-64 and 3.08% at 65+, while male characters' words are 3.75%, 19.65%, 31.90%, 39.27% and 5.42%.

source: For men, it’s the exact opposite: there are more roles available to older actors.
claim: Male characters number 549 under 21, 2,233 at 21-31, 3,564 at 32-41, 5,449 at 42-64 and 968 at 65+, while female characters number 451, 1,932, 1,581, 1,281 and 253.

source: Even films with female leads, such as Mulan, the dialogue swings male.
claim: Mulan's dialogue is 75.31% male and 24.69% female.
The Truman Show's dialogue is 87.11% male and 12.89% female.
